- Whether Redwood’s subprocessors (particularly logging & analytics) will see cleartext customer data or only pseudonymized records

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@novamed.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Sep 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood - SCC alignment + TIA scoping questions

Oliver —

Appreciate the clear asks. I’ll put together a concise packet that covers: SCC/UK addendum usage, the current subprocessor exposure model, and an explicit TIA recommendation (scope + recommended safeguards).

High level now: Redwood serves customers under the EU Commission SCCs (2021) by default for EU->US exports and we offer a UK IDTA addendum where UK personal data is involved. Our platform enforces separation between application payloads and telemetry; most analytics/logging data is pseudonymized or tokenized by default, though certain infra-level logs (crash traces, kernel-level metrics) are retained in a limited-access subprocessor. I’ll confirm names and access modes in the packet.

I’ll loop in Legal Ops and our infra lead to validate access patterns and provide the subprocessor inventory. Plan to send by COB Monday (22 Sep).

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Privacy & Compliance Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Sep 2025 12:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Redwood - SCC alignment + TIA scoping questions — need quick inputs

Evelyn — quick answers below; I attached the live subprocessor export (CSV) as requested.

- Logging/metrics: Sentry (error traces) and Datadog (infra metrics) see partial traces; payloads are redacted by default but crash traces can include small snippets of user-generated text when exceptions occur. Access to crash traces is tightly role-based and audited.
- Analytics: Snowplow only receives pseudonymized event keys; no PII is stored in analytics datastore.
- CDP/Customer telemetry: Segment is used for routing of customer-defined telemetry (customer opt-in). For enterprise customers we support masking at the SDK level.
- KMS: Customer-managed keys supported for Dedicated & Private deployments; hosted customers default to Redwood-managed KMS.

Plaintext exposure: there are two rare cases where infra-level diagnostics may include customer textual snippets — we have a documented redaction play and limited retention window (30 days) for those traces.

Attached: subprocessor-inventory-20250921.csv

—Kim
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@novamed.com>, PrivacyOps <privacyops@novamed.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Sep 2025 17:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood - SCC alignment + TIA scoping questions

Oliver / Privacy team —

Thanks for the patience. Attached are: (1) redwood-scc-summary.pdf (one-page summary of when we rely on EU SCCs and the UK IDTA addendum), (2) tia-flowchart.png (recommended TIA scope & decision tree), and (3) subprocessor-inventory-20250921.csv (export of subprocessors and access modes). High-level conclusions:

- Transfer mechanism: For EU data we rely on the EU Commission SCCs (2021). For UK personal data we will execute the UK IDTA/UK addendum when customers request it or if requirements in their contract/policy require it.
- Subprocessor exposure: Most analytics/telemetry is pseudonymized. Sentry/Datadog may receive limited, redacted textual snippets for diagnostics. We apply strict role-based access and maintain a 30-day retention window for infra traces that contain any textual payload.
- TIA recommendation: Given the current technical controls (pseudonymization for analytics, km-s options for Dedicated/Private, short infra trace retention, strict RBAC + audit logs) we recommend a scoped TIA (logistics & backup storage excluded) with the following additional safeguards for NovaMed:
  * Customer-managed KMS or double-wrapping for any EU->US key ops
  * Contractual commitment to 30d max retention on infra traces containing text
  * Optional route policy to keep sensitive workloads in EU-only Dedicated capacity

Next steps: if you want the legal team to sign a bespoke TIA we can draft language; otherwise the SCCs + the above contractual commitments should address the majority of enterprise concerns.

Please confirm whether you want a drafted TIA and we’ll route a first-pass to your counsel.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Privacy & Compliance Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-scc-summary.pdf (1 page), tia-flowchart.png (diagram), subprocessor-inventory-20250921.csv (CSV)
